subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 6-year-old boy develops fever, abdominal pain, and bloody diarrhea after eating undercooked meat. Over the next two days he becomes pallid and lethargic. Laboratory studies show anemia and thrombocytopenia, with fragmented helmet-shaped cells on peripheral smear, elevated LDH, and indirect hyperbilirubinemia. Which morphologic finding on the smear is most consistent with microangiopathic hemolytic anemia?
question: Fragmented helmet-shaped cells on peripheral smear in microangiopathic hemolytic anemia are called:
explanation_correct: Schistocytes (helmet cells) are fragmented RBCs produced by mechanical shearing in microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, such as DIC, TTP/HUS, and HELLP syndrome, or by mechanical hemolysis from a prosthetic heart valve. The vignette of anemia with thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, and hemolysis markers fits TTP/HUS. Recognizing schistocytes points to a microangiopathic or mechanical cause rather than a membrane or hemoglobin defect.

explanation_incorrect.B: Spherocytes are small spherical cells without central pallor, seen in hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Target cells have increased surface area-to-volume ratio and are seen in HbC disease, asplenia, liver disease, and thalassemia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Acanthocytes are spur cells with asymmetric projections, seen in liver disease, abetalipoproteinemia, and vitamin E deficiency.
explanation_incorrect.E: Elliptocytes are oval cells seen in hereditary elliptocytosis due to membrane protein (spectrin) mutations.

educationalObjective: Schistocytes are fragmented helmet cells of MAHA (DIC, TTP/HUS, HELLP) or mechanical valve hemolysis.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 24-year-old man of Mediterranean ancestry develops jaundice and dark urine two days after eating fava beans. Laboratory testing shows acute hemolytic anemia with Heinz bodies on supravital stain and bite-shaped cells on the peripheral smear. Which enzyme deficiency underlies this condition?
question: Bite cells (degmacytes) on peripheral smear are characteristically associated with deficiency of which enzyme?
explanation_correct: In glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, oxidative stress such as fava beans or certain drugs causes hemoglobin to denature and precipitate as Heinz bodies. Splenic macrophages remove these Heinz bodies, producing bite cells (degmacytes) on the peripheral smear. This is an X-linked disorder and a classic cause of episodic hemolysis with jaundice and dark urine.

explanation_incorrect.A: Pyruvate kinase deficiency causes hemolytic anemia with echinocytes (burr cells), not bite cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency is von Gierke disease (glycogen storage disease type I), not a hemolytic anemia with bite cells.
explanation_incorrect.D: Spectrin mutations cause hereditary elliptocytosis and hereditary spherocytosis, not bite cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: Bilirubin UDP-glucuronyltransferase deficiency causes Gilbert or Crigler-Najjar syndrome, not hemolysis with bite cells.

educationalObjective: Degmacytes (bite cells) indicate G6PD deficiency after splenic macrophages remove Heinz bodies.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A researcher examines peripheral smears from two patients with liver disease. One smear shows RBCs with irregularly sized projections at uneven intervals, while the other shows smaller, uniformly sized, evenly spaced projections. Which cell type displays the asymmetric, irregular projections?
question: Which RBC morphology is characterized by projections of varying size at irregular intervals (asymmetric spur cells)?
explanation_correct: Acanthocytes (spur cells) have projections of varying size at irregular intervals and are asymmetric; they are associated with liver disease, abetalipoproteinemia, and vitamin E deficiency. Echinocytes (burr cells) are the key contrast: their projections are smaller, uniform, and evenly spaced, and they occur in liver disease, ESRD, and pyruvate kinase deficiency. Distinguishing asymmetric from uniform projections is the point of this comparison.

explanation_incorrect.A: Echinocytes (burr cells) have smaller, uniform, evenly spaced projections and are seen in liver disease, ESRD, and pyruvate kinase deficiency.
explanation_incorrect.B: Target cells show increased surface area-to-volume ratio and a bull's-eye appearance, associated with HbC, asplenia, liver disease, and thalassemia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Spherocytes are small spherical cells lacking central pallor, with decreased surface area-to-volume ratio.
explanation_incorrect.E: Schistocytes are fragmented helmet cells from microangiopathic or mechanical hemolysis.

educationalObjective: Acanthocytes have asymmetric irregular spur projections; echinocytes have uniform even burr projections.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 62-year-old man with progressive anemia and splenomegaly has a peripheral smear showing teardrop-shaped RBCs along with circulating nucleated RBCs and immature granulocytes (a leukoerythroblastic reaction). Bone marrow biopsy reveals extensive fibrosis. Which term describes the teardrop-shaped RBCs?
question: Teardrop cells (dacrocytes) on peripheral smear are most strongly associated with which condition?

options.text: Bone marrow infiltration such as myelofibrosis

explanation_correct: Dacrocytes (teardrop cells) result from RBCs being mechanically squeezed and deformed as they exit a fibrotic or infiltrated bone marrow; they are a hallmark of marrow infiltration such as myelofibrosis and are often accompanied by a leukoerythroblastic reaction with immature granulocytes and nucleated RBCs. The mnemonic is that the RBC sheds a tear because it is squeezed out of its home in the marrow.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hereditary spherocytosis produces spherocytes, not teardrop cells.
explanation_incorrect.C: Iron deficiency anemia produces microcytic hypochromic cells with increased central pallor, not dacrocytes.
explanation_incorrect.D: Sickle cell anemia produces sickled cells and target cells, not teardrop cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia is associated with spherocytes, not dacrocytes.

educationalObjective: Dacrocytes (teardrop cells) signal marrow infiltration/myelofibrosis, often with a leukoerythroblastic reaction.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 14-year-old girl has anemia, jaundice, and a family history of similar episodes. Peripheral smear shows many small, round, densely staining RBCs that lack central pallor, and osmotic fragility is increased. Which RBC morphology is described?
question: Small spherical RBCs lacking central pallor are called:
explanation_correct: Spherocytes are small, spherical RBCs without central pallor and have a decreased surface area-to-volume ratio. They are the classic morphologic finding in hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Their reduced membrane surface area makes them less deformable and prone to sequestration and destruction in the spleen.

explanation_incorrect.A: Target cells have a central area of hemoglobin, a pale ring, and a dark outer rim, with increased surface area-to-volume ratio.
explanation_incorrect.B: Schistocytes are fragmented helmet cells from microangiopathic hemolysis, not smooth spheres.
explanation_incorrect.C: Elliptocytes are oval or elliptical cells seen in hereditary elliptocytosis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Acanthocytes are spur cells with irregular asymmetric projections.

educationalObjective: Spherocytes are small spheres without central pallor (HS and AIHA) with decreased surface area-to-volume ratio.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 45-year-old woman who underwent splenectomy 5 years earlier has a routine smear showing RBCs with a central area of hemoglobin, a pale ring, and a dark outer rim (a bull's-eye appearance). Which of the following correctly describes this morphology and its surface area-to-volume ratio?
question: Target cells (as in HbC disease, asplenia, liver disease, or thalassemia) have which of the following characteristics?

options.text: Decreased surface area-to-volume ratio; seen in hereditary spherocytosis
Increased surface area-to-volume ratio; associated with HbC, asplenia, liver disease, thalassemia
Uniform projections; seen in pyruvate kinase deficiency

explanation_correct: Target cells have excess membrane relative to cell volume, giving an increased surface area-to-volume ratio and a bull's-eye appearance on smear. The classic associations are remembered by HALT: HbC disease, Asplenia, Liver disease, and Thalassemia. This contrasts with spherocytes, which have a decreased surface area-to-volume ratio.

explanation_incorrect.A: Decreased surface area-to-volume ratio describes spherocytes (hereditary spherocytosis and AIHA), not target cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Fragmented cells are schistocytes, seen in microangiopathic hemolysis such as DIC.
explanation_incorrect.D: Asymmetric projections describe acanthocytes, seen in abetalipoproteinemia and liver disease.
explanation_incorrect.E: Uniform projections describe echinocytes, seen in pyruvate kinase deficiency, ESRD, and liver disease.

educationalObjective: Target cells have increased surface area-to-volume ratio; HALT = HbC, asplenia, liver disease, thalassemia.

subject: Oncology and Hematology
vignette: A 68-year-old man has fatigue and macrocytosis with an MCV of 112 fL. The peripheral smear shows large, oval RBCs, and the differential includes neutrophils with six nuclear lobes. Bone marrow examination shows megaloblastic changes. Which peripheral smear finding is most characteristic of megaloblastic anemia?
question: Macro-ovalocytes with hypersegmented neutrophils on peripheral smear are characteristic of which anemia?
explanation_correct: Macro-ovalocytes (large, oval RBCs) together with hypersegmented neutrophils with five to six lobes are the hallmark peripheral smear findings of megaloblastic anemia due to vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, which impair DNA synthesis. The high MCV reflects continued cytoplasmic growth with defective nuclear maturation. This distinguishes megaloblastic from nonmegaloblastic causes of macrocytosis such as liver disease or chronic alcohol overuse.

explanation_incorrect.B: Iron deficiency anemia is microcytic and hypochromic with increased central pallor, not macrocytic with macro-ovalocytes.
explanation_incorrect.C: Sickle cell anemia shows sickled cells and target cells, not macro-ovalocytes or hypersegmented neutrophils.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hereditary spherocytosis shows spherocytes without central pallor, not macro-ovalocytes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia shows schistocytes (fragmented RBCs), not macro-ovalocytes.

educationalObjective: Macro-ovalocytes plus hypersegmented PMNs indicate megaloblastic anemia from B12 or folate deficiency.
